1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing around the short text elements.

2.why: No italics or all-caps appear anywhere; headings are sentence case and the longest text is a single short sentence.

3.why: Content sits in a single narrow centred column with large fields and buttons that reads cleanly at small widths, though actual mobile rendering is not shown.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Enter the six-digit code delivered to your verified mobile number' are one short sentence in essentially plain language.

5.why: No placeholder or worked example is shown for the email, phone, or code fields; the only guidance is the phrase 'six-digit code'.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is a single sentence, so no long block of reading is ever required to proceed.

7.why: No long code or secret is ever displayed for copying in these screens; the only code arrives by SMS and must be keyed into the field by hand.

8.why: No QR code or any alternative to manual entry appears; the flow stalls at SMS verification and never reaches the authenticator setup step.

9.why: There is no password field and nothing in the plain inputs demonstrates autofill or password-manager support.

10.why: Each screen has a bold step heading ('Sign in to begin', 'Verify your identity') and one solid blue primary button that clearly dominates the page.

11.why: Each step presents a single primary button, though the first step asks for two pieces of information (email and phone number) at once.

12.why: Successful action feedback appears only as a low-prominence 'Logs' entry ('Identity verification delivery was initiated'), while failure produces an inline error, so outcomes are stated but not plainly or prominently.

13.why: After the error the form remains usable and 'Please try again' invites retry with no visible lockout or penalty, though there is no reveal/hide toggle and no option to re-request the code.

14.why: The only error message, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', avoids blaming the user but never states what the problem actually was or how to fix it beyond retrying.

15.why: No countdown, timer, or expiry warning appears on any screen, so no time pressure on reading or entry is observable.
